fit: ginger powder capsules and first postoperative bowel movement
assessment: Ginger versus placebo shortened time to first defecation after abdominal hysterectomy by a reported 12.6 hours, 95% CI 4.5–20.8. Acute postoperative recovery has no measured bridge to chronic constipation severity with grated ginger in Parkinson disease.

fit: ginger capsules with enhanced recovery and postoperative ileus
assessment: Ileus occurred in 23 of 80 per arm, and first flatus was similar. Defecation data were incomplete. This is a countercomparison for the postoperative context, with a different care protocol and no chronic constipation result.

fit: rhizome extract and upper gastrointestinal pressure activity
assessment: The 12-person healthy-participant original reports phase III antral and postmeal corpus motor activity. Manometry does not quantify stool, constipation or grated-root exposure.

fit: dried ginger suspension and esophageal motility
assessment: The fixed-order healthy-participant comparison found increased sphincter relaxation at swallowing and lower esophageal wave speed at several timepoints. The original tables measure esophagus, with no colonic endpoint.

fit: fresh ginger motion tolerance and dried ginger liquid emptying
assessment: Fresh and powdered ginger showed no clear motion tolerance benefit. The liquid-emptying comparison used 500 mg powder and was inconclusive despite partial change in electrical activity. Constipation severity was not measured.

fit: ginger capsules and postoperative stool timing
assessment: Ginger versus placebo after cesarean delivery gave a secondary first stool about 5.9 hours earlier, with reported p=.048, and constipation adverse-event counts of 13 versus 17. This brief postoperative setting differs from chronic Parkinson bowel symptoms and grated ginger.

fit: Parkinson bowel diary and safety in a separate botanical drug trial
assessment: Stool frequency and Bristol class did not show clear changes. Two constipation adverse events versus zero were reported separately. DA-9701 contains Corydalis tuber and Pharbitis seed, and the study supplies no ginger contrast.

fit: Parkinson constipation scale and solid gastric emptying
assessment: Domperidone use was associated with faster gastric emptying without a clear change in constipation in an 11-person uncontrolled study. This human Parkinson result distinguishes endpoints but supplies no ginger estimate.

fit: ginger capsules and postoperative pain scores
assessment: The enhanced-recovery trial showed no clear difference in epigastric pain or postoperative pain scores after hysterectomy. The surgical setting and capsule preparation do not provide a Parkinson pain contrast.

fit: Parkinson upper abdominal pain diary in a separate botanical drug trial
assessment: The drug-first group had a four-week within-group diary p=.029 for burning or upper abdominal pain. The placebo-first value was p=.216. These are within-group comparisons, and the formulation has no ginger.
